title: This Beetle Smells a Dead Mouse From 2 Miles Away, Then Buries It
subject: burying beetle

scenes.text: A beetle smells a dead mouse from two miles away.
Burying beetles find small carcasses, often within about an hour of death.
Then a pair strips the fur, rolls the body into a ball, and coats it so it rots slower.
Burying it takes around eight hours, hidden underground from rivals.
The female lays eggs beside it. Both parents feed the hatched larvae from their own mouths.
If there are too many hungry larvae, the parents eat some. A mouse. A nursery. A buried grave.

description:
A burying beetle can smell a small dead animal from up to two miles away.
A pair strips it, rolls it into a ball, buries it for their young, and may eat extra larvae if food runs short.
What is the strangest parent in the animal world?
first_comment: This beetle buries a mouse for its babies. Would you stick around to see the nursery? What insect parent surprised you most?
